newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, gold up, PGMs down.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, gold up, PGMs down.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures ended higher Wednesday on some light fund and trade buying, while NYMEX platinum group metal (PGM) futures ended lower after another claim by Russia's export agency, Almaz, that talks would resume on the Russia/Japan supply contract stalled since last December.
COMEX June gold ended 90 cents at $342.40 an ounce, recovering from a three day low seen Tuesday. Estimated total volume was a relatively modest 17,000 lots.
After an outside-range day Tuesday, in which June gold tested both sides of its $340-345 range of the past month, the contract was seen continuing to consolidate in narrow ranges, traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.00/50, compared with the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $341.10 and the New York close Tuesday around $340.30/80.

"It is not unreasonable to suggest the gold market after the first quarter of this year is showing some of the characteristics which led to the bull market of 1993," Gold Fields Mineral Services Ltd (GFMS) analyst, Philip Klapwijk, said at an analysts briefing in New York.
"A number of parallels are undoubtedly there, such as the depressed price, and the resulting record levels of physical offtake from the gold markets of Asia," he said.
"The physical market has now kicked in with a vengeance and is once again providing a rather solid floor at the $340 level in spite of the continued strength of the dollar."
But many analysts remain concerned about the potential for further European central bank gold sales ahead of the introduction of European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
World official sector gold sales rose for the third consecutive year to 588 tonnes in 1996, according to the GFMS 1997 annual gold market survey published Wednesday.
But GFMS argued that net sales were only 239 tonnes, the highest for three years, but lower than in 1992 and 1993.

Overnight Wednesday, the Dutch central bank again denied it was currently selling gold or even active in the gold swaps or derivative markets, after talk of renewed European central bank activity this week.

COMEX July silver ended up 2.5 cents at $4.758, with support still seen around $4.70 and resistance around $4.80, after July silver recovered from contract lows at $4.630 seen on April 28. Estimated total COMEX silver volume was a low 10,000 lots.
NYMEX July platinum settled down 10 cents at $372.90 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium lost $1.20 to end at $155.00 an ounce.

In overnight news, Russian metals export agency deputy director, Sergei Gorney, said he saw talks with Japan on the resumption of PGM supplies from Russia resuming soon. Talks on the supply contract broke down last December.
But PGM lease rates remained high, with nearby palladium futures in backwardation, and physical market prices were tending to be higher than nearby futures market prices, traders said.
